hero.eyebrow: TRACK INTELLIGENCE // BETA · SAMPLE DATA · POWERED BY PYXIS-1
hero.sub: PYXIS-1 measures rhythm, energy, harmony, timbre, spectral behaviour and structure — 70+ measurable audio characteristics — and organises them into one readable track profile. Evidence first, interpretation alongside.
hero.anatomyLabel: SONIC ANATOMY · ONE RECORDING, MANY MEASUREMENTS
hero.figureAlt: Sonic anatomy instrument: a track waveform acts as the central spine of the diagram. Analysis lanes are layered around it — structure sections, an energy contour, a harmony strip, a timbre ridge and an identity row. Selecting a lens brings one lane forward while the others recede, and a plain-language interpretation of that layer appears below. Sample data.
hero.title: See how the track moves, changes and [[holds together.]]

profile.title: One track. One readable profile.
profile.lead: The first level of analysis — a concise professional summary, before any chart asks for your attention.
profile.miniAlt: Compact profile strip: the track's six sections as blocks with the energy contour drawn above them. Sample data.
profile.tableAlt: Key measurements with their source: measured values come directly from the audio, predicted values are classification signals with confidence
profile.interp: A steady, club-oriented track with a long central breakdown, stable tempo and its highest sustained energy in the final drop. Measured values are read directly from the audio; predicted values are classification signals, shown with confidence.

structure.title: How the track unfolds
structure.lead: A structural score — waveform, beat grid and sections on one timeline. Select a section to read its role.
structure.panelLabel: STRUCTURAL SCORE · WAVEFORM + BEAT GRID + SECTIONS
structure.figureAlt: Structural score: the full waveform with a beat grid beneath it and six labelled section blocks — intro, build, drop 01, break, drop 02, outro — with their durations. The selected section is highlighted with its energy and loudness readout. Sample data.

energy.title: How energy moves through the track
energy.lead: One continuous energy journey — loudness and dynamic range layered beneath it, anchored to the structure.
energy.figureAlt: Layered dynamics chart: a shaded dynamic-range band, a grey loudness contour and a white energy contour drawn over section markers. The global peak in the final drop is marked in orange. Sample data.
energy.readingInterp: Reading it: intensity climbs gradually — no abrupt jumps; the long break releases energy before the strongest section; the final drop carries the global peak, then the outro steps down rather than cutting.
energy.body: DJs read the internal movement before set preparation. Producers study arrangement and intensity. Curators assess pacing. Catalogue teams turn the journey into searchable energy descriptors. The analysis describes the track — the decision stays yours.

harmony.title: Key and harmonic behaviour
harmony.lead: Detected key, confidence and a readable chromagram strip up front — full pitch evidence and harmonic relationships one step deeper.
harmony.interp: The track stays centred on G minor throughout, with its strongest tonal movement during the break — pitch content spreads before the final drop re-anchors the key.
harmony.tonalAlt: Harmonic field: a key-agreement line across the six sections that dips during the break, above a compact chromagram strip of the twelve pitch classes over time — G and B-flat dominate. Sample data.
harmony.chromaAlt: Chromagram: twelve pitch-class rows across the track timeline. Cells brighten where a pitch class carries more energy; G and B-flat dominate, with wider spread during the break. Sample data.

spectral.title: The texture of the recording
spectral.lead: A branded spectral terrain — sub to air — with the brightness contour and texture regions read in plain language.
spectral.terrainAlt: Spectral terrain: a spectrogram field from sub frequencies at the bottom to air at the top across the track timeline, rendered in greys with orange marking the hottest regions. A brightness contour is drawn over it, rising at the final drop. Sample data.
spectral.timbreLabel: timbre evolution · band balance over time
spectral.timbreAlt: Timbre evolution: stacked bands showing how the balance between sub, body, presence and air changes across the track — sub-weighted early, presence and air widening at the final drop. Sample data.
spectral.mfccAlt: MFCC timbral fingerprint: thirteen coefficient cells summarising the track's texture. Sample data.
spectral.textureInterp: Texture read: dark and dense through the first half — smooth, sub-weighted, percussive; the final drop lifts brightness and opens the top end without losing weight.
spectral.body: Described as measured character — dark or bright, dense or open, smooth or percussive, stable or evolving. Never as a verdict on the mix.

identity.title: A profile, not a label
identity.lead: Genre, style, mood and vibe as coordinated signals — stronger and weaker, never absolute.
identity.vibeBody: Compositional indicators from the analysis — instrumentation balance and phrasing character as shown in the current dashboard.
identity.legendAlt: Confidence envelope legend: solid orange marks strong signals, solid grey marks supporting signals, dotted outlines mark uncertain or overlapping signals
identity.overlapInterp: Primary classification: deep house. Secondary characteristics suggest tech house and minimal influences — the profile keeps the overlap visible instead of forcing one answer.

confidence.title: Measured, interpreted, never presented as absolute.
confidence.lead: Classification is contextual. Styles overlap. Confidence stays visible, and every number traces back to the analysis that produced it.
statements: Measured values (tempo, key, loudness, structure) are read directly from the audio and are deterministic — the same file returns the same profile.
Predicted values (genre, style, mood, vibe) are classification signals — shown with confidence, with secondary signals kept visible.
Similar styles overlap; the profile presents the overlap instead of hiding it behind one label.
Raw charts never stand alone — each carries a plain-language interpretation.
Every result is traceable to its analysis run — engine version, date and scope.
